text:
alex: vuln-bot just flagged CVE-2025-2319 in tokenizers (<=0.13.3) — potential RCE via malformed input. see vuln-bot message below.

vuln-bot: AUTO: CVE-2025-2319 detected in dependency tokenizers@0.13.3. Affected package: tokenizers. Severity: HIGH. Recommended: upgrade to patched release >=0.13.4 or apply backported patch. Link: https://cve.example/CVE-2025-2319

maria: thanks for the ping. quick question — do we vendor tokenizers anywhere in infra or use it only in model-serving containers?
alex: only in model-serving images and a few devtools. runtime spin: hosted-api uses transformers 4.35 with tokenizers 0.13.3 pinned via poetry.lock. Dedicated/private images get their own buildpack but same base.
sam_g: triage notes — the exploit vector needs input validation bypass; still plausible in our public endpoints that accept free text (notably prompt upload APIs). we should treat as high.
kevin: agreed. plan: 1) verify impact by running fuzz on staging images, 2) prepare poetry.lock update and a tiny compatibility PR, 3) run full CI + canary deploy to Dedicated.
maria: FYI we recently had a CI flake when upgrading starlette -> 0.26 in the last release branch. if the lock update pulls a newer starlette/fastapi transitive, CI might break again. we should pin transitive versions in the PR.
sam_g: good call. i ran `poetry show --tree` on the service and tokenizers is pulled directly by transformers; fastapi/starlette are separate. still, resolver sometimes picks different starlette for unrelated upgrades.
alex: proposing immediate mitigation: add a runtime WAF rule to sanitize prompt payloads + rate-limit uploads while we patch. low-friction stopgap.
kevin: sounds fine. who's owning the patch PR? @maria?
maria: i can do the PR. steps i'm planning:
```
# create branch
git checkout -b fix/tokenizers-cve-2025-2319
# update lock only for tokenizers via poetry
poetry add tokenizers@^0.13.4 --lock
# pin starlette & fastapi to current known-good versions
poetry add 'starlette==0.25.0' 'fastapi==0.95.2' --lock
# run tests
pytest services/model-serving/tests -q
```

sam_g: couple of notes: 1) use `poetry lock --no-update` only to avoid grabbing other upgrades; 2) we should run a minimal smoke in staging container with `python -m http.server` style harness to test ingestion path.

alex: CI failure we hit previously (from last starlette bump) looked like this:``
E   TypeError: __init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'scope'
/opt/venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/starlette/somefile.py:42
```

maria: i'll try the lock update locally and see if that error reproduces in tox/py311. if it does, i'll try pinning only starlette for the PR and add a CI job that runs the subset of integration tests in parallel to speed iteration.

vuln-bot: REMINDER: If you ship a patch, attach SLSA provenance info for the build to the PR for Private customers.

sam_g: priority: P0 for hosted API, P1 for offline devtools. i can handle the fuzzing on staging tonight — will report results in this thread.

kevin: timeline: patch PR + security review today, run CI and canary by tomorrow noon PST. if CI fails because of starlette/fastapi, fallback is to ship a hotfix image where we rebuild transformers with a vendored patched tokenizers wheel.
maria: noted. I'll open the PR with the minimal lock change and an explict changelog entry referencing CVE-2025-2319. PR will include the following checklist: [x] fuzz results attached, [x] smoke tests, [ ] canary plan, [ ] SLSA provenance.
alex: Thanks. tag me on the PR and i'll coordinate ops to hold the canary window and WAF rule.

sam_g: quick status update: fuzzing produced a crash on staging tokenizer.decode() with malformed bytes — reproducible. attaching snippet to PR when i open it.
maria: i opened https://github.com/redwood-inference/model-serving/pull/512 with the lock update and pinned transitive deps. requesting review from @kevin and @alex.

kevin: reviewing now. one comment: add a temporary CI marker `security-patch` to run the faster subset first, we can block merge until all green.

alex: sounds good. after merge we'll schedule a canary to 5% traffic for 2h then 25% if stable. post-canary rollback plan: automatic fallback to previous container image via router policy.

maria: PR merged. CI passed the fast subset, full CI running. i'll post results.
sam_g: fuzzing logs attached to PR — crash case is non-exploitable without a race on how we allocate KV cache, but still unacceptable.

vuln-bot: STATUS: CVE-2025-2319 marked MITIGATED for repository model-serving after PR #512 merged. Please confirm canary outcomes.

alex: canary started at 1803456950. tagging this thread for incident log.

kevin: canary 5% for 2h -> no errors. increasing to 25% now.

maria: full CI passed. will coordinate with support to update customer advisory draft.

sam_g: closing fuzz findings as 'mitigated' pending long-term patch upstream. i'll keep an eye on transformer/tokenizers upstream PRs.

alex: great work team. I'll file a short postmortem note in /incidents after the canary completes. :trophy:
